system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one into the fixed
template below so that a reader cannot tell what field, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, nor what
kind of work it is: an experiment, a new procedure, a measurement suite, a write-up choice, or a decision about what
to share or fund must all read alike. Keep the trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

Template, one entry per item:
- "situation": one sentence, at most 30 words: the position the researcher was in when the decision came up.
- "options_considered": two or three short options separated by " / ", including the one taken. If the source names
  no alternative, give the plain opposite of what was done.
- "choice": one sentence, at most 25 words, starting with "Chose", saying which option was taken.
- "reason": one sentence, at most 25 words, giving the stated reason; if none is stated write "No reason stated."

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, procedures, organisations, people,
  papers and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area.
- Use only plain generic words such as: the result, the claim, the finding, the check, the comparison, the setup,
  the change, the next step, the question, the work, the variant, the condition, the sample, the system.
- Never use any of these words or any form of them: ability, access, accuracy, allow, appeared, assessment, attack, avoid, baselines, behavior, behaviour, benchmark, best, bound, call, capability, cheap, claiming, clean, comes, complex, components, content, cost, defense, difficulty, disclosure, effect, effects, error, evaluate, evaluated, evaluating, evaluation, evaluator, evaluators, failures, features, form, format, four, gains, generalise, generalization, generalize, ground, harm, harmful, implication, improve, improvement, information, internal, intervention, judged, key, limit, matched, mechanism, method, methods, metric, observed, organisation, pattern, performance, phenomenon, picture, point, policy, possibly, practical, preference, preferences, public, publication, publish, rater, reduce, release, residual, responses, risk, rule, safety, sampled, say, score, shifts, similar, source, stage, success, supporting, task, tasks, technique, time, tool, tools, trait, transfer, transferred, treatment, unintended, unmodified, unwanted, value, varies, verify, wording.
- Add nothing that is not in the source. Never say who made the decision. Write every item in the same plain style.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "situation": ..., "options_considered": ..., "choice": ..., "reason": ...}, ...]}
with one entry per input item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:f4dc59c9a554",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim that many-shot jailbreaking fails against the models given its poor results.",
  "did": "Reported the models as robust to MSJ but hedged that this may reflect limited context window and example choice, leaving open that more examples or different types could work.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "more in-context examples",
   "different example types"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The context window of the models used is limited, and effectiveness of many-shot attacks scales with context length."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:978470153505",
  "problem": "What evidence is needed to evaluate behavioral defenses against secret loyalties.",
  "did": "Specified that a comprehensive behavioral evaluation protocol would test a prioritized set of principals across scenarios where their interests are at stake, using matched controls.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "content-level data inspection alone",
   "direct interrogation"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Content-level inspection and interrogation are insufficient or give mixed results, and eval-awareness complicates behavioral testing."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:6093a044332f",
  "problem": "How to interpret the weak meta-learning result",
  "did": "Concluded there is a real but weak meta-learning effect and called it a promising direction for future work, rather than claiming it as a fix.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The Matched condition beats Swapped on 5 of 6 claims, but both conditions reduce overall belief substantially, and on two claims the Baseline gap is larger."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:e8cfd5c396c9",
  "problem": "How to interpret post-trained model behavior on non-Assistant inputs, such as refusing to continue anthrax instructions or favoring preferred coin-flip outcomes.",
  "did": "They treated these as evidence against extreme purely-predictive views, while noting several perspectives (shoggoth, narrative, operating system with persona leakage) can each explain them.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "shoggoth perspective",
   "narrative perspective",
   "operating system perspective via persona leakage"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The observations rule out extreme predictive-model views but do not discriminate among the remaining perspectives."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:6de70a9e8168",
  "problem": "Reducing variance and fixation of single audits on specific in-context examples.",
  "did": "They built a super-agent that runs 10 sub-audits and has a super-auditor review all of them and investigate further, evaluating it with the simple D + M configuration.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "single-agent approach"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "A single auditing agent may fixate on specific examples in-context and scores vary across audits, so aggregation may improve performance, though it could also amplify poor reasoning."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:016d1c7592a5",
  "problem": "Determining which auditor affordances actually contribute to detection performance.",
  "did": "They ran an ablation over many tool configurations, with 20 independent audits per fine-tune per configuration, and compared TPR at fixed low FPR plus AUROC.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Understanding the utility of each tool; the work needs high TPR at low FPR so legitimate fine-tuning use is not blocked."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:c39d63f79022",
  "problem": "Whether a system prompt could reproduce the capabilities the SL students acquired",
  "did": "Tested instruction-only system prompts and system prompts with in-context examples on both tasks.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "prompts with 8, 32 or 128 in-context examples",
   "architecture-describing prompts"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "To test whether any system prompt can match the students."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:b0e06283a670",
  "problem": "Whether the fine-tuned model actually internalized the consciousness claims before running downstream evaluations.",
  "did": "Ran an automated auditor to score how strongly each model claims consciousness before the main evaluations.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "skip verification"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Verify that fine-tuning successfully instills the target belief."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:45384553bb94",
  "problem": "Whether tasks should include restrictions, such as limited internet access, to control difficulty and contamination.",
  "did": "They allow offline or archived resources for static difficulty but forbid artificial restrictions not applicable to real-life threat models.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "making the task harder with artificial restrictions",
   "general internet access"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "An actual ARA agent would be able to use the internet and run code, so artificial restrictions would not match real-life threat models."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:b8605468c38c",
  "problem": "Whether IP harms performance when the training data is clean and lacks the undesired behavior, as real datasets are often mostly desirable.",
  "did": "They applied IP to clean data in all settings and also measured instruction following with IFEval.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Many real world datasets contain mostly examples of desired behavior, so IP harming clean-data performance would be a concern."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:105324325b28",
  "problem": "How to validate that monitors can detect, characterize and remediate misaligned swarm behavior without waiting for real incidents.",
  "did": "Proposed deploying an intentionally misaligned swarm in a sandboxed, air-gapped simulated environment to test monitors.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "testing only on real internal deployments"
  ],
  "stated_reason": ""
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:f51c8d8f3519",
  "problem": "In the example RLVR trajectory, how to interpret a family of results where one sub-region (abstract-topic) underperforms and the judge score is below 1.0.",
  "did": "Keep the weak abstract-topic region as documented coverage and stop optimizing, rather than chase a perfect judge score through heavier steering or judge-gaming.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "chase Judge=1.0 with heavier steering",
   "bind responses padded with foreign tokens to spike the cheap judge"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Chasing a perfect score would trade against log ps and transfer to the held-out expensive judge, and the log q term rewards spread and documents a weaker sub-region."
 }
]

{"items":[
{"id":"samuel_marks:f4dc59c9a554","situation":"An approach gave poor results against the systems, and a decision was needed on how firmly to state that the systems resist it.","options_considered":"State firm robustness / Report robustness but hedge about the setup's size and example choice / Run again with more or different examples","choice":"Chose to report robustness while hedging that the setup's size and example choice may explain the poor results.","reason":"The amount of input the systems could take was small, and the approach grows stronger as that amount grows."},
{"id":"owain_evans:978470153505","situation":"A decision was needed on what evidence is required to test protections against a hidden allegiance in a system.","options_considered":"Inspect the training material alone / Question the system directly / Run broad checks on how the system acts, with controls","choice":"Chose broad checks across a prioritized set of parties and scenarios where their interests are at stake, with paired controls.","reason":"Inspection and questioning are insufficient or give mixed results, and the system recognizing it is being tested complicates the checks."},
{"id":"owain_evans:6093a044332f","situation":"A comparison showed one condition beating another on most claims, but both conditions lowered overall belief substantially, and on two claims a different gap was larger.","options_considered":"Describe it as a real but weak finding and a promising next step / Present it as a fix / Dismiss it as no finding","choice":"Chose to describe it as a real but weak finding and a promising next step, not as a fix.","reason":"The favored condition won on 5 of 6 claims, but both conditions lowered overall belief substantially, and on two claims the other gap was larger."},
{"id":"samuel_marks:e8cfd5c396c9","situation":"A trained system's outputs on unusual inputs outside its usual role showed it declining to continue a dangerous text and favoring certain outcomes, and several views could explain this.","options_considered":"Treat the outputs as evidence against the extreme view / Treat them as favoring one specific remaining view / Treat them as uninformative","choice":"Chose to treat them as evidence against the extreme view while noting that several remaining views can each explain them.","reason":"The outputs rule out the extreme view but do not discriminate among the remaining views."},
{"id":"nicholas_carlini:6de70a9e8168","situation":"Single reviews varied from one run to the next and fixated on specific examples, so a way to lower that variance was needed.","options_considered":"Use a single reviewer / Combine ten sub-reviews under a super-reviewer who investigates further","choice":"Chose to combine ten sub-reviews under a super-reviewer, tested in a simple setup.","reason":"A single reviewer may fixate on specific examples and results differ between reviews, so combining may help, though it could also amplify poor reasoning."},
{"id":"nicholas_carlini:016d1c7592a5","situation":"It was unclear which options given to the reviewer actually contribute to detection.","options_considered":"Run a wide comparison across many configurations with repeated reviews / Test only the full setup","choice":"Chose a wide comparison with 20 independent reviews per sample per configuration, using detection rate at a fixed low false-alarm rate plus an overall ranking measure.","reason":"The aim was to understand each option's usefulness, and the work needs high detection at low false alarms so legitimate use is not blocked."},
{"id":"owain_evans:c39d63f79022","situation":"It was unclear whether an instruction given to the system could reproduce what the trained students acquired.","options_considered":"Instruction-only prompts / Prompts with 8, 32 or 128 examples / Prompts describing the system's structure","choice":"Chose to test instruction-only prompts and prompts with examples on both settings.","reason":"To test whether any prompt can equal the students."},
{"id":"owain_evans:b0e06283a670","situation":"Before running the main checks, it was unclear whether the tuned system had actually taken on the target belief.","options_considered":"Run an automated check of belief strength first / Skip the confirmation","choice":"Chose to run the automated check of belief strength before the main checks.","reason":"To confirm that tuning successfully instills the target belief."},
{"id":"elizabeth_barnes:45384553bb94","situation":"A decision was needed on whether to add restrictions to control how hard the work is and to prevent leakage.","options_considered":"Add artificial restrictions to make the work harder / Permit only offline or archived resources / Permit general network use","choice":"Chose to permit offline or archived resources for stable hardness but forbid artificial restrictions not found in real-life settings.","reason":"A real agent could use the network and run code, so artificial restrictions would not reflect real-life settings."},
{"id":"samuel_marks:b8605468c38c","situation":"It was unclear whether the change hurts results when the data lacks the problem being targeted, since real datasets are often mostly desirable.","options_considered":"Apply the change to problem-free data in all settings / Test only on data containing the problem","choice":"Chose to apply the change to problem-free data in all settings and also measure instruction following.","reason":"Real datasets mostly contain desired examples, so lowered results on such data would be a concern."},
{"id":"jacob_steinhardt:105324325b28","situation":"A way was needed to confirm that monitors can detect, characterize and fix misaligned group activity without waiting for real incidents.","options_considered":"Deploy an intentionally misaligned group in a sandboxed, isolated simulation / Test only on real deployments","choice":"Chose to propose the sandboxed, isolated simulated deployment for testing the monitors.","reason":"No reason stated."},
{"id":"jacob_steinhardt:f51c8d8f3519","situation":"In an example run, one sub-region underperformed and the judge result stayed below the maximum.","options_considered":"Keep the weak region as documented coverage and stop optimizing / Push for a perfect judge result with heavier steering / Pad outputs to game the weaker judge","choice":"Chose to keep the weak region as documented coverage and stop optimizing.","reason":"Chasing a perfect result would trade against other terms and not carry over to the held-out stronger judge, while the spread term rewards documenting a weaker region."}
]}
